executive_assessment.text: Kintampo assessment examples distinguish selected-community exposure and adaptive capacity; rankings from nine purposively selected communities cannot be generalized nationwide.
Gushegu adds a conditional heat/resource-pressure mechanism mediated by tenure and dispute institutions; political and identity dynamics remain central.
Regional profiles and warning-system arrangements add capacity detail, without proving effective warning reach or reduced losses.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024-12 reports: The BTR reports vulnerability rising from coastal zones through the transition belt to northern savannas; Upper West is highest, while Greater Accra, Ashanti and Central are lowest across 216 districts and six ecological zones.

Source dated 2024-03 reports: The assessment ranks Busuama, Dawadawa and Alhassan Akura as Kintampo’s most vulnerable communities and Kintampo least; Busuama combines low capacity, rainfed livelihoods, weak service/market access and flood-prone homes.

Source dated 2024-03 reports: Kintampo and Cheranda scored high in adaptive capacity, linked to credit, remittances, markets, irrigation, crop diversity and extension; Busuama, Dawadawa, Alhassan Akura and New Longoro scored very low.

Source dated 2024-03 reports: The assessment identifies Cheranda, Babato, Dawadawa and New Longoro among Kintampo communities most affected by bushfires, which damage vegetation and crops including cashew.

Source dated 2022-12-09 reports: In Gushegu, the author links heat stress and resource scarcity to herders’ mobility and feeding adaptations that damage crops or breach tree tenure and can trigger farmer-herder disputes.

Source dated 2022-12-09 reports: A Gushegu chief-led committee hears farmer-herder disputes and may decide compensation, but is informal and cannot enforce decisions; some parties distrust its decisions or allege favoritism.

Source dated 2025-12-23 reports: The strategy assigns coastal flood/sea-level-rise risk to Greater Accra, Volta and Central; river flooding to Northern, Upper East and Eastern; drought and heat to Northern, Upper East, Upper West and Savannah.
The December 2025 strategy's regional composite rates coping capacity very low in Savannah, North East, Oti and Northern and very high in Greater Accra.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 17 of 17 evidence records and 2 of 2 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
The CCDR's regional discussion of climate-related migration and social vulnerability was not coded as a country-specific FCV pathway.
A larger UNFCCC communication and national adaptation plan did not open in the web reader; their direct PDFs were not used.
The northern Ghana brief's 2080 migration/conflict risk does not specify the projection scenario.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The official Ghana National Adaptation Plan linked from the UNFCCC record could not be inspected because its 18.1 MB PDF exceeded browser retrieval limits; no claims use its metadata or indexed text.
The inspected reverse-FCV search did not locate evidence that armed conflict disrupted climate-adaptation delivery; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
Kintampo community rankings derive from 153 households in nine purposively selected communities and should not be generalized to the municipality or Ghana.
The source-reported farmer-herder mechanism in Gushegu is conditional and multi-causal; no independent national climate-conflict estimate was found.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
